subject: Request: mid-cycle seat rollback + credit note (Ornatek)
messages:
From: María López <maria.lopez@ornatek.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@ornatek.com
Date: 2027-04-19 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Request: rollback of mid-cycle seat add + credit note

Hi Hannah,

Quick one — we mistakenly auto-approved a 5-seat increase on Apr 4 that we no longer need. Can you please roll that change back to our previous 12-seat commitment (so net -5 seats) and issue a credit for the portion of April we were charged?

Relevant docs attached: Ornatek PO 4521 (for the upgrade) and our internal payment hold note. We also need a VAT-visible credit note (we operate under reverse-charge in the Netherlands). I can share our VAT ID if you need it.

A couple constraints: our AP team has a temporary payment hold until the credit is issued — they'll release payment for the balance on the current invoice once the credit memo is visible. Please advise expected timeline.

Thanks,
María López
Head of Ops, Ornatek
maría.lopez@ornatek.com

Attachments: ornatek_po_4521.pdf (pdf), payment_hold_note.txt (txt)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19 10:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: rollback of mid-cycle seat add + credit note

Hi María — thanks for the heads up and for sending the PO. We can handle the rollback and credit, and I’ve looped in Jordan (your AM) and Kimberly from Billing to coordinate the calculation and the formal credit memo.

To make sure we do this cleanly:
- Can you confirm the exact date you want the rollback effective? Based on your note it sounds like you want to revert to the pre-Apr-4 seat count (i.e., remove the 5 seats added on Apr 4).
- Do you prefer the credit applied to the next invoice or issued as a refund to the original payment method? (You mentioned your AP hold; applying to next invoice is quicker in many cases.)
- Please send your EU VAT ID if you want the credit memo to reflect reverse-charge (0% VAT) — Kimberly will need that to generate the VAT-compliant document.

We’ll aim to turn around the calculation and a draft credit memo same day once Kimberly confirms.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales (EMEA) | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: María López <maria.lopez@ornatek.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19 10:42:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: rollback of mid-cycle seat add + credit note

Hi María — Jordan here. I pulled the usage and billing windows and sketched a quick prorate so you have visibility before Kimberly issues the formal credit memo. Assumptions below — please correct if any differ:

- Monthly billing period: Apr 1 — Apr 30 (30-day month basis used internally)
- Upgrade effective: 2027-04-04 (5 seats added)
- Request rollback effective: 2027-04-18 (we’ll treat this as the date you stopped using the additional seats per your note)
- Seat price (list): €120.00 / seat / month (your committed seat rate)
- Seats to remove: 5

Prorate math (illustrative):
Days charged for added seats: 2027-04-04 through 2027-04-17 = 14 days
Prorated fraction: 14 / 30 = 0.4667
Monthly charge for 5 seats: 5 * €120 = €600.00
Prorated charge for that partial period: €600 * 0.4667 ≈ €280.00

Because we billed the full seat add on the Apr invoice, the credit we should issue (gross) is approximately €320.00 (billing included a short rounding and a prior-day overlap; Kimberly will produce exact numbers) — final gross credit will appear on the credit memo.

VAT note: if you confirm your EU VAT ID and that reverse-charge applies, the credit memo will be issued with 0% VAT and reference your VAT ID. If no VAT ID is provided, we’ll issue with Dutch VAT at the applicable rate and that will change the net vs gross totals.

I’ve attached a quick spreadsheet showing the day-by-day breakdown. Kimberly — can you prepare a credit memo (PDF) with the formal credit_memo number and indicate whether we should post the credit to Ornatek’s account or refund to the original card on file? María, for speed, applying to next invoice will release your AP hold sooner.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: proration_calculation.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: María López <maria.lopez@ornatek.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19 11:10:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: rollback of mid-cycle seat add + credit note

Hi María — thanks for the PO and the context. I’ve generated a provisional credit memo and adjusted the April invoice draft. Key items: 

- Credit memo #: CR-ORNT-20270419-02
- Gross credit (pre-VAT): €320.00
- VAT handling: pending your VAT ID. If you confirm Ornatek VAT ID and reverse-charge applies, the credit will be issued at 0% VAT and reference your VAT number on the memo. If not, we will apply Dutch VAT at 21% which will change the memo total.
- Application: Per Jordan’s note, I recommend applying the credit to the next invoice to clear Ornatek’s outstanding balance quickly and allow AP to release the payment hold. If you prefer a refund, please confirm the refund bank details and allow 5–7 business days for processing.

I’ve attached the formal credit memo (credit_memo_ORNT-20270419.pdf) and included a breakdown of the day-level proration.

Action needed from Ornatek: please reply with either 
1) Confirm apply credit to next invoice (preferred), OR
2) Confirm refund to original payment method and provide bank details.
Also please send your company VAT ID so I can reissue the memo with the correct VAT treatment.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: credit_memo_ORNT-20270419.pdf

AP will release the payment hold once the credit memo is posted and the adjusted invoice is visible in our portal. No refund needed.

Appreciate the speedy help.
